title: #thesharkisbroken #thesharkisbrokenbroadway #thesharkisbrokenbway #ja...
transcript: Last night I saw The Shark Is Broken on Broadway, a comedy that follows Robert Shaw, Roy Scheider, and Richard Dreyfus over the course of the making of the movie Jaws. I gotta be honest, it really wasn't for me. I kind of figured this might be primarily a vanity project, which is fine, but parts of the script just seemed really self. And honestly, the making of the movie jaws feels pretty superfluous. About most of the play, it's mostly just the 3 of them trauma bonding and Pickering on this boat they had to live on for weeks. I couldn't find any stakes in the plot, so it was also hard to be invested. Now all these things I could have theoretically looked past, but the nail in the coffin for me was that it just wasn't very funny. I had a chuckle here and there, especially from Alex brightman's great performance. And it's not like it was terrible by any means, but there are just much funnier and more interesting shows to see right now. If you've seen it and you think I'm crazy, please let me know your thoughts. I would love to hear them. But to me, it just wasn't that funny. And in this economy, when I go to a comedy, I want to laugh hard and consistently. With that, another playbill for my collection.
reasoning: Clear negative recommendation with multiple criticisms (not funny, no stakes, vanity project feel) and explicit comparison that there are 'much funnier and more interesting shows to see right now.'
